counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].r from 0.6946 to 0.2. This reduces radius below corner distance, so no overlap occurs and collision handling is no longer required; scenario passes, showing failure is due to insufficient corner penetration resolution for large radius.

explanation: Body falls diagonally past thin wall's top edge. At step 33 it grazes the top-left corner (9.1,5.0) with distance -0.032 (within tolerance). Next step 34 it penetrates to -0.156, exceeding 0.15 limit. This is a corner collision: closest point is wall corner, not face. Collision detection appears to use axis-aligned distance or miss corner normals, so impulse/positional correction fails to prevent corner tunneling when vertical speed dominates (~7.4 m/s) and radius is large (0.694). Reducing radius to 0.2 removes overlap, confirming penetration depth is radius minus corner distance.
vision_note: A red circle drops vertically onto the top of a thin dark vertical wall. In steps 31-33 it sits just above the tip, but in step 34 it overlaps and sinks into the wall, showing wall penetration.
